channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: 10 new photo and video apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These camera and editing apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Photo & Video charts this week, from film-look cameras and a VHS camcorder to a teleprompter and a RAW editor.

item.title: 10 new productivity apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These productivity apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Productivity charts this week, from a handwriting notebook and a talking keyboard to planners, countdowns and a shift calendar.

item.title: 10 new travel apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These travel apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Travel charts this week, from a gas price finder and Connecticut's mobile ID to translators, cruise port guides and a plane radar.

item.title: 10 new weather apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These weather apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Weather charts this week, from 3D storm radar and hurricane prep to northern lights odds and snow forecasts.

item.title: 5 new lifestyle apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These lifestyle apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's paid Lifestyle chart this week, from a pocket typewriter for letters to a Christmas countdown and a private journal.

item.title: 7 new music apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These music apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Music charts this week, from record and cassette players for your Apple Music library to a free drum machine and a four-track recorder.

item.title: 7 new utility apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These utility apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Utilities charts this week, from widgets and a keyboard for the foldable iPhone Duo to Google Wallet's new iPhone app.

item.title: 9 new health and fitness apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These health and fitness apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's paid Health & Fitness charts this week, from a step graph for the Apple Watch and a running app to a newborn log and breathing exercises.

item.title: Firefox iOS Gecko engine: why Firefox on iPhone still uses WebKit
item.description: Mozilla says Apple's EU rules would make it ship Firefox with its own Gecko engine as a separate new app instead of an update, so iPhone users would have to move bookmarks, passwords and history by hand. For now Firefox on iPhone stays on Apple's WebKit.

item.title: Fitbit vs Google Health app: what changed for Fitbit users in 2026
item.description: In 2026 the Fitbit app became the Google Health app, Fitbit accounts gave way to Google accounts, and from 28 November third-party apps and clock faces can no longer be installed on Fitbit watches.

item.title: Google Assistant vs Gemini for Home: what changes on your speakers
item.description: Google Assistant stops working on Google's smart speakers and displays on 2 August 2027 and the Nest app closes on 25 January 2027, so Nest owners move to the Google Home app and Gemini for Home, with some features behind a Home Premium plan from $10 a month.

item.title: Googlebook vs Chromebook: what Google's new laptops mean for you
item.description: Googlebooks are Android-based laptops from $899 that went on sale in October, while existing Chromebooks keep getting updates for their supported lifetime, with ChromeOS patches promised through mid-2034.

item.title: WhatsApp video call scam: fake bank and FCA staff, police warn
item.description: Nottinghamshire Police in England say they've had a rise in reports of fraudsters on WhatsApp messages, voice calls and video calls who claim to be from a bank or the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Some victims lost hundreds of pounds.

item.title: 7 minute workout app FitIn7: one $0.99 purchase, no subscription
item.description: FitIn7 is a new iPhone and iPad app for a 7-minute bodyweight workout at home, sold for $0.99 once with no subscription, ads or account. It came out on 21 November and was #25 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: AI phishing emails: TheMailer kit rewrites scams until they pass spam filters
item.description: Security firm Varonis found TheMailer, a phishing kit sold to criminals that uses AI services such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini to write scam emails and keeps rewriting them until they land in the inbox instead of spam. Good grammar is no longer a sign that an email is real.

item.title: Alexa Plus explained: cost, free with Prime, devices and countries
item.description: Alexa+ is Amazon's AI version of Alexa: it's included with Prime and costs $19.99 a month without it in the US, it's open to everyone in the US and Canada, and this year it has reached 11 more countries through early access, Japan last on 29 October.

item.title: Amazon Prime gas discount Fridays: 20 cents off at BP until 29 January
item.description: Amazon Prime members who link an earnify account get 10 cents off a gallon every day at BP, Amoco and participating ampm and Thorntons stations in the US, and 20 cents off on Fridays until 29 January. The Friday price counts for one fill-up of up to 35 gallons.

item.title: Apple AI agent may not come before late 2027, Gurman says
item.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman doesn't expect Apple's AI agent, which would click and type its way through apps and websites for you, before the end of 2027 at the earliest. Apple hasn't announced the agent.

item.title: Aurora wallpaper app makes your own abstract wallpapers on iPhone and Mac
item.description: Aurora – Wallpaper Studio draws abstract wallpapers on your own device from 16 styles, each in a light and a dark version, for $14.99 once across iPhone, iPad and Mac. It was #33 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: Breathwork app for athletes: Second Wind adapts to your sleep and HRV
item.description: Second Wind is a new iPhone app, out since 18 November, with guided breathing for athletes that adapts each session to last night's sleep, the day's training and your HRV and resting heart rate against your own baseline. It costs 2.99 dollars once, with no subscription or account.

item.title: Discord new app Phoenix spotted in Android alpha test
item.description: Discord's rebuilt app, code-named Phoenix and written in Rust, is already inside the Android alpha version next to the current app, Notebookcheck reports; it's limited to Discord staff for now, and Discord hasn't given a release date.

item.title: Fitbit Air notifications: Cuff app makes the band buzz for calls
item.description: The Fitbit Air has a vibration motor, but Google only uses it for silent alarms. Cuff, an Android app built by a Reddit user, connects to the band over Bluetooth and makes it vibrate for calls, chosen contacts and apps like Slack and Telegram.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: shorter answers, admit doubt less in test
item.description: In Artificial Analysis' personality test, OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra gave answers 40% shorter than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol 34% shorter than GPT-6.1 Sol, but both scored much lower on admitting uncertainty, The Decoder reports. The scores describe answer style, not whether answers are correct.

item.title: GTA 6 AI photo prompt trend: turn a selfie into a GTA poster in ChatGPT
item.description: Since GTA 6 came out, people are turning their selfies into neon Vice City posters with ChatGPT or Gemini and posting them on Instagram; brands use the look too. All it takes is a photo and a prompt.

item.title: Hello Moon: ambient music app for iPhone that follows the Moon's phase
item.description: Hello Moon plays ambient music that changes with the Moon's current phase, with its own composed themes for each of the eight phases. The $3.99 app came out on 7 November and was #31 in Music on the US App Store's paid chart on 22 November.

item.title: Hex voice to text keyboard for iPhone: dictate in any app, free
item.description: Hex is a free voice to text keyboard for iPhone that turns your speech into text right where you're typing, in any app, with no account or subscription. It was #51 among free Productivity apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: How to turn off AI features in Canva, Gemini and Signal explained
item.description: In one week Canva added a switch that turns off its generative AI tools, Google split Gemini's settings so you can keep chat history but stop AI training, and Signal began blocking screenshots so phone assistants can't read your chats, but each switch covers less than its name suggests.

item.title: iOS 27 Connectivity Assist: iPhone uses cellular when Wi-Fi is weak
item.description: iOS 27 has a switch called Connectivity Assist that lets your iPhone use cellular data when the Wi-Fi it's connected to is slow or unusable. You find it in Settings, Wi-Fi.

item.title: iPhone Duo Lock Screen widgets: Apple tested an extra column, leak says
item.description: According to the leaker pdfu, iOS 27.1 contains a hidden "Complication Column" that puts two round widgets, one above the other, on the right edge of the iPhone Duo's Lock Screen. It's switched off, and Apple hasn't said whether it will ship.

item.title: iTell app: use your Android phone's second number on your iPhone
item.description: iTell connects an Android phone to your iPhone over Bluetooth, so you can take and make its calls, read and answer its texts and see its contacts from the iPhone. The free iPhone app came out on 8 November and was #55 in Utilities on the US App Store's free chart on 22 November.

item.title: Keepy Uppy Job Tracker: log jobs and send invoices if you're self-employed
item.description: Keepy Uppy Job Tracker is a new $2.99 iPhone app for self-employed people that logs a finished job in one tap and tracks who still owes you money. It was #15 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: Location history app for iPhone keeps your timeline in iCloud
item.description: Private Location History, a 99-cent iPhone app, records the places you visit and the trips between them as a daily timeline that stays on your device and your own iCloud, without an account. It was #58 in Travel among paid apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: MacBook Apple logo light: Backglow app lets you turn it off or dim it
item.description: Backglow is a Mac app that lets you dim, switch off or animate the glowing Apple logo on the back of the new MacBook Pro with the PROLED XDR display, which macOS has no setting for. The basic modes are free.

item.title: Metro Global transit app: live arrivals in the Americas and Europe
item.description: Metro Global is a 99-cent iPhone app that shows nearby stations, schedules, live arrivals and departure boards for transit in the Americas and Europe. It was #35 among paid Navigation apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: Noticed app: practice small talk and communication skills on iPhone
item.description: Noticed is a free iPhone and iPad app that teaches communication skills with lessons, quizzes, small-talk video scenarios and a speech analyzer that tells you how you sound. It was #87 among free Education apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: Outlook outage report: emails to inactive inboxes bounced
item.description: Microsoft's final report on the 12 November Microsoft 365 outage says delayed emails to personal Outlook inboxes that hadn't been used for more than 30 days expired, and their senders got a non-delivery notice. Work and school emails were all delivered in the end.

item.title: Paste Snippets iCloud sync: saved text on iPhone, iPad and Mac
item.description: Paste Snippets, a keyboard app from iDownloadBlog that puts your saved bits of text under the keyboard, now keeps those snippets the same on iPhone, iPad and Mac through iCloud. Apple encrypts them in your iCloud.

item.title: Personalized children's book made with AI, printed as a hardcover
item.description: papergarden is a new website that writes and illustrates a picture book with your child as the hero, then sells it as an eBook for €9.95 or a hardcover for €39 plus shipping.

item.title: Siri AI daily limit explained: what counts and how to get more
item.description: With iOS 27.3, Siri AI keeps simple requests unlimited but pauses multi-step and writing requests once a device hits its daily limit, and only an iCloud+ plan of 200 GB or more raises that limit, much like Gemini and ChatGPT tie heavier use to paid plans.

item.title: Spotify AI remix feature: ready, but no release date yet
item.description: Spotify's finance chief Christian Luiga said the tool that lets fans make AI covers and remixes is ready, but no users have tried it yet, because Spotify still needs consent from enough individual artists. He gave no launch window and no price.

item.title: Windows 11 lets antivirus run outside the kernel to cut blue screens
item.description: Microsoft's new Windows endpoint security platform, now generally available on Windows 11, lets security apps do their checks outside the Windows kernel, so a faulty update is less likely to crash the PC. Bitdefender Antivirus Free and Sophos plan support by the end of 2026.

item.title: Apple Siri settlement claim: about $61 per iPhone, deadline December 21
item.description: US buyers of an iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model can claim money from Apple's $250 million Siri settlement until December 21. Lawyers for the buyers estimated on November 16 that each eligible iPhone will likely get at least $61, with $95 as the most per phone.

item.title: Billable Timer app: track billable hours on iPhone and iPad
item.description: Billable Timer: Time Tracker is a $4.99 app for people who bill by the hour, such as lawyers, accountants and consultants, with no in-app purchases. It was #33 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 22 November.

item.title: Clicks Communicator delay: keyboard phone now ships in 2027
item.description: Clicks has moved deliveries of its $649 Communicator keyboard phone from December to late January and February 2027. People who ordered before 20 November get a pair of 3.5mm wired headphones in the box.

item.title: Copilot will rename and move files for you on Windows 11
item.description: Microsoft showed at Ignite 2026 that Copilot will soon move, rename and sort files in folders like Downloads and Desktop when you ask in plain words. Microsoft calls it local file actions and hasn't given a date.

item.title: Dayclipse app: sunrise, golden hour and moon phase tracker
item.description: Dayclipse: Sun & Moon Tracker is a $4.99 app that shows sunrise, sunset, golden hour, blue hour and moon phases for any place, and works offline. It was #29 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Digital ID at TSA explained: Apple Wallet, Google Wallet, state apps
item.description: You can show a digital ID on your phone at TSA checkpoints in more than 250 US airports, by tapping the reader or scanning a QR code, but TSA still wants every traveler to carry a physical ID as well.

item.title: Doxology Way prayer app: daily prayers for five Christian traditions
item.description: Doxology Way is a $9.99 daily prayer app that follows the prayers, readings and saints of the tradition you pick: Orthodox, Catholic, Anglican, Lutheran or Protestant and Evangelical. It was #55 among paid Reference apps on the US App Store on 21 November.

item.title: Fitbit third-party apps and clock faces end on November 28
item.description: From 28 November you can't install or update third-party apps and clock faces on Fitbit Sense and Versa watches; only Fitbit's and Google's own stay in the gallery. What's already on your watch keeps working, but a deleted app or a factory reset means it's gone for good.

item.title: Gemini camera on Android redesigned: it now opens inside your chat
item.description: The camera you open from the plus menu in Gemini's prompt box now slides up as a sheet over your chat on Android, instead of a separate full-screen viewfinder. It has rolled out widely with Google app version 17.76 and later, after reaching the iPhone app first.
